subject.title: [Feature]: Self-evolving SOUL.md via opt-in reflection sub-turn + soul_update tool

question: Should OpenClaw accept core, default-off SOUL.md auto-evolution, or should durable preference capture stay in memory/plugin surfaces instead?
rationale: The request is missing and has a clear implementation candidate, but it adds model-mediated writes to a prompt-loaded instruction file plus new config and CLI surfaces.

options.title: Accept guarded core contract
options.body: Keep this issue canonical and review the linked PR only after private tool gating, provenance, escaping, visible notice, undo, and hostile-input coverage are satisfactory.

options.title: Route to memory or plugin
options.body: Reject direct SOUL.md mutation in core and ask for durable preference capture through memory plugins or a new plugin/API seam.

options.title: Decline automatic mutation
options.body: Close this issue and the older overlapping issue if maintainers do not want model-mediated instruction-file writes at all.

recommendation.title: Accept guarded core contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical and review the linked PR only after private tool gating, provenance, escaping, visible notice, undo, and hostile-input coverage are satisfactory.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans SOUL docs, prompt assembly, core runtime/config boundaries, and security posture, all areas represented in this handle's path history.
